subsystems.name: Agent platform
subsystems.role: the individual robot or drone that senses, moves and communicates.

subsystems.name: Local communication
subsystems.role: lets nearby agents share state without a central server.

subsystems.name: Coordination algorithm
subsystems.role: turns simple local rules into complex collective behaviour.

subsystems.name: Perception and localisation
subsystems.role: each agent must know where it is and what its neighbours are doing.

subsystems.name: Human–swarm interface
subsystems.role: lets an operator set goals, monitor progress and intervene.

buildSteps.title: Define the collective goal
buildSteps.detail: Specify the mission (e.g. area search, package relay, environmental sampling) and the constraints on time, energy and safety.

buildSteps.title: Design the agent
buildSteps.detail: Choose or build a robot with the sensing, mobility and communication needed for that mission; keep it simple and cheap so many can be fielded.

buildSteps.title: Write local interaction rules
buildSteps.detail: Each agent gets rules for how to respond to nearby agents and to the environment — for example move toward neighbours but keep a set distance, or leave a digital mark when a area is searched.

buildSteps.title: Implement the communication layer
buildSteps.detail: Set up a mesh network or stigmergic medium so agents can exchange only local information; avoid any single point of failure.

buildSteps.title: Simulate at scale
buildSteps.detail: Run thousands of virtual agents to test emergence, robustness and failure modes before touching hardware.

buildSteps.title: Validate with a small physical swarm
buildSteps.detail: Test with a handful of real robots in a controlled space to calibrate sensors, timing and communication range.

buildSteps.title: Scale up incrementally
buildSteps.detail: Add agents in stages, checking that the collective behaviour remains stable and that failures degrade gracefully.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with human oversight
buildSteps.detail: Operate the swarm under an operator who sets high-level goals, monitors the swarm and can recall it if needed.

prerequisites.why: agents must communicate peer-to-peer without relying on fixed infrastructure.
small, cheap robots are needed to make large swarms practical.
onboard processing lets agents react quickly without sending data to a central server.
rules that work in simulation often break when real robots face noise, delays and failures.
flight time and run time limit how long a swarm can operate.

pathway.milestone: centralised fleets of warehouse robots and pre-programmed drone light shows
pathway.unlocks: commercial experience with many robots at once, though coordination is still largely centralised.

pathway.milestone: decentralised swarms for inspection, agriculture and delivery in controlled areas
pathway.unlocks: lower cost and greater resilience because no single controller directs every agent.

pathway.milestone: search-and-rescue swarms that map disaster zones and locate survivors with human oversight
pathway.unlocks: faster response in places too dangerous or too large for individual robots.

pathway.milestone: fully autonomous swarms for logistics and environmental monitoring
pathway.unlocks: scalable, self-organising systems that adapt to changing conditions without constant human input.
